title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan dan memahami teks tentang pengalaman liburan di masa lalu.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 78-79
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about how long actions took on vacation in the past using “How long did …?”.
Learners will be able to speak and write about the length of a stay and travel time using “stayed for …” and “took …”.
Learners will learn the importance of being responsible and prepared when going on a vacation.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 78.
First, the teacher reads the questions in the speech bubble at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the questions aloud as a class.

Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs (e.g. “How long did you stay at the resort?” – “We stayed for two weeks.”, “How long did the bus ride take?” – “The bus ride took eight hours.”).
Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary in the questions (e.g. the hotel, the village, the plane journey).

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different things. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.
To finish the speaking activity, elicit responses from some students by asking the questions in the speech bubbles with the original vocabulary, and also with some substituted vocabulary.

Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes), e.g. “stayed for six days” (not “stayed six days”) and “took 90 minutes” (not “took for 90 minutes”).
Ask students to look at Speaking and Writing B on Student Book page 78 and read the examples and the questions aloud together as a class.
Put students in pairs. Tell them to ask and answer the questions, using the information in (parentheses) to answer, and to write their partner’s answers in complete sentences.

Remind them to follow the structures shown in the Q&A models and Language Box: “stayed + for + time” and “took + time” (e.g. “They stayed in the village for four days.”, “The bus ride took ninety minutes to get there.”).
Give students around 10 minutes to complete the task, then check the answers as a class and write them on the board.
Put students in new pairs to practice asking and correctly answering the questions. Student A asks first, then switch roles, focusing on pronunciation and intonation.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Write these questions on the board: “Where did you go?”, “How long did it take you to get there?”, “How long did you stay?”
Put students in pairs to take turns asking and answering the questions about their own past vacations.

Remind students to use full sentences and the correct past verbs, following the Q&A models and Language Box on Student Book page 78 (e.g. “I went to my grandparents’ village. The car ride took three hours. We stayed for six days.”).
If there is extra time, students can switch partners and repeat the activity. Ask some students to share their partner’s answers with the class.
Direct the students to look at the picture on page 79 and ask them “What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.

Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value (Being responsible and prepared). They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think this skill (or value) is important when we go on vacation?”
Ask students to look at activity A and read the instructions as given on the page. Ask some instruction-checking questions to check if students understand the task.
Ask students to work in groups, discussing each action and whether it shows being responsible and prepared, before putting a tick or a cross in the box.
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do, then give students around 5 minutes to complete the task.
Check the answers and write them on the board. Ask students to explain why each action is (or is not) responsible.
Ask students to look at activity B.

Put students into groups of three or four and ask them to agree on the 5 most important things to pack for a vacation to each place: the beach, the mountains, the city, and the forest. Students write their answers on the lines.
Show the beach example if needed: “When we went to the beach, we needed to pack … sunscreen – to protect our skin from the sun.”
Give students around 10-12 minutes to complete this task.
Elicit some answers from different groups about what they would pack. There is no need for every group to give answers for every place, because they will share more in the next activity.
Ask students to look at Activity C.

Tell each group to share with the class which important items they needed to pack for each place, and say why those items were important, using “We needed … because …” (e.g. “We needed warm jackets because it was very cold.”).
If there is limited time, assign each group one place (the beach, the mountains, the city, or the forest) so that the groups don’t all talk about the same place.
Finish the activity by asking students which of the places they would prefer to go to, and why.
Wrap up the class by highlighting that being responsible and prepared, such as planning ahead and packing the right things, helps us stay safe and enjoy our trips.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
